chapters.title: Your freelance offer
chapters.blurb: Decide what you sell and say it clearly. Everything later is built from this.

lessons.title: Define your freelance offer
lessons.summary: Turn your technical skills into one service a client can understand: what you build, who needs it, and the problem it solves.

parts.title: Why an offer beats a skill list

lessons.output: A freelance offer saved to your profile. Later lessons reuse it for your bio and platform profiles.

blocks.title: Clients buy outcomes, not stacks
blocks.body:
Clients do not search for a tech stack. They have a problem.

As a {{role}}, say what you do in their words:

- **What** you build
- **Who** it is for
- **Which problem** it solves

One service is enough to start.

blocks.title: Skill list versus offer
blocks.body:
Skill list: “JavaScript, Python, SQL.”

Offer: “I build small internal tools for teams that run their work in spreadsheets, so routine tasks stop taking hours.”

body_by_specialization.websites:
Skill list: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript, WordPress.”

Offer: “I build fast, simple websites for local service businesses, so customers can find them and book without calling.”
body_by_specialization.web_apps:
Skill list: “React, Node.js, PostgreSQL.”

Offer: “I build customer dashboards for small SaaS teams, so their users can manage accounts without emailing support.”
body_by_specialization.mobile_apps:
Skill list: “Swift, Kotlin, React Native.”

Offer: “I build booking apps for fitness studios, so members can reserve classes from their phone.”
body_by_specialization.backend:
Skill list: “Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Docker.”

Offer: “I build and repair APIs for small product teams, so their app stays fast as more customers sign up.”
body_by_specialization.automation:
Skill list: “Python, Zapier, APIs.”

Offer: “I automate reporting for small e-commerce teams, so the weekly numbers arrive without anyone copying data by hand.”

lessons.title: Spot a strong offer
lessons.summary: Train your eye: tell a clear, client-ready offer from a vague one, then check your own.

parts.title: Three signs of a strong offer

lessons.output: A passed check and one rule you will apply to your own offer.

blocks.title: Three signs of a strong offer
blocks.body:
Read a freelancer's first line and ask:

- **Can I picture the client?**
- **Do I know what changes for them?**
- **Is it one thing?**

Specific and modest beats impressive and vague.

questions.prompt: Which first line would a client understand fastest?

options.label: Full-stack developer: React, Node.js, AWS, Docker, Kubernetes
I build online booking systems for small clinics so patients stop calling to schedule
Passionate coder available for any project

questions.explanation: It names what is built, who it is for and what changes. The other two describe the developer, not the client's problem.

questions.prompt: You have only built practice projects. What is the honest way to show experience?

options.label: Describe them as client work so they look stronger
Show the practice project and label it as practice

questions.explanation: Real, labeled practice work is proof you can build. Invented client work is a risk the first time a client asks about it.

questions.prompt: Your offer lists six different services. What is the best next step?

options.label: Pick the one you can prove best and lead with it
Add four more so every client finds something
Replace the list with “anything you need”

questions.explanation: One service you can back with evidence is easier to trust and easier to find.

actions.title: Lead with one service
actions.instructions: If your saved offer covers more than one service, narrow it.

lessons.title: Write your professional bio
lessons.summary: Turn your offer into a short bio you can reuse on every platform: who you help, what you do, your evidence, and how to start.
lessons.output: A professional bio saved to your profile, ready to adapt for your platforms.

blocks.title: The four-part bio
blocks.body:
A bio is your offer with a little more room:

1. **Who you help**
2. **What you do for them**
3. **Your evidence**
4. **How to start**

Write it the way you would say it out loud. You will adapt it for {{channel}} later.

blocks.title: Only what is true
blocks.body: No clients, results or years you do not have. Short and honest wins.

fields.name: evidence
fields.label: Your evidence
fields.help: Real work. Label practice as practice.

fields.name: how-to-start
fields.label: How to start working with you
